newsitem.title: USA: Solv-Ex acted correctly in Fiba deal-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex acted correctly in Fiba deal-CEO.

text.p: Solv-Ex Corp chairman and chief executive John Rendall said the firm believes it acted correctly in its private placement of shares through London brokerage Fiba-Nordic Securities.

In a conference call, Rendall said Solv-Ex had conducted a thorough review of the transaction and acknowledged he was aware of a connection between Fiba-Nordic and the Morgan Grenfell Asset Management funds formerly run by Peter Young.
The review, he said, showed Solv-Ex acted properly in all aspects of the placement.

"After a review of the situation with the parties concerned over the last 10 days, and our own records, Solv-Ex believes it has acted correctly, repeat correctly, in all aspects of the transaction," Rendall said.
"In addition," Rendall added, "we repeat that to our knowledge, the management, officers and directors of Solv-Ex are not the subject of any SEC or other investigation."

In early March, Solv-Ex placed about 1.1 million common shares through Fiba-Nordic for a total of about $30.69 million. Less than two weeks later, it placed a second tranche of shares for identical terms through the same firm.

Within days of the second placement, the shares came under heavy selling pressure on published reports of a U.S. federal probe into allegations that international traders had artificially pumped up the company's share price.
On March 31, Solv-Ex said it had learned of two federal inquiries into possible manipulation of its share price. Solv-Ex said it supported the probe and would cooperate.
Last month, the company announced it had filed suit in federal court in New York, alleging short-sellers in the company's shares had disseminated false information about the company's technology.
Solv-Ex is seeking to implement its techniques for extracting oil and alumina from oil sands on land it is leasing in Alberta.
Rendall said the company continues to expect to be "producing oil for the marketplace with the specifications available to market it in the first quarter of next year."

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, a U.K.-based subsidiary of Deutsche Bank AG, said early Thursday that the three funds suspended early in the week had resumed trading. Last night, the firm won an injunction freezing the personal assets of former fund manager Peter Young.
